src: 店内でお召し上がりですか
ja: 店内でお召し上がりですか
kana: てんないでおめしあがりですか
english: for here?; are you eating in?
use: Asked at fast-food and café counters; answer hai, or mochikaeri de (to go).

example.romaji: tennai de omeshiagari desu ka, omochikaeri desu ka?
example.ja: 店内でお召し上がりですか、お持ち帰りですか？

notes: Meshiagaru is the respectful verb for eat and drink.

use: Asked at fast-food, café and bento counters; answer hai, or tennai de (for here).

example.romaji: omochikaeri desu ka? fukuro ni oire shimasu ne.
example.ja: お持ち帰りですか？袋にお入れしますね。
example.english: To go? I'll put it in a bag.

notes: To ask for it yourself, say mochikaeri de onegai shimasu. Some places say teikuauto.

kana: おすきなせきへどうぞ
use: Staff say it when there are free tables; just pick one.

example.romaji: ohitori desu ne. osuki na seki e douzo.
example.ja: お一人ですね。お好きな席へどうぞ。
example.english: Just one? Sit anywhere you like.

src: お下げしてもよろしいですか
ja: お下げしてもよろしいですか
kana: おさげしてもよろしいですか
romaji: osage shite mo yoroshii desu ka
english: may I take your plate?; may I clear this?
use: A waiter asks before clearing dishes; answer hai, onegai shimasu, or mada desu (not yet).

example.romaji: kochira, osage shite mo yoroshii desu ka?
example.ja: こちら、お下げしてもよろしいですか？

notes: Sageru here means to clear away.

kana: ただいまうかがいます
english: I'll be right with you; coming right away
use: Staff call it back when you say sumimasen! and they're busy; just wait a moment.

example.romaji: hai, tadaima ukagaimasu. shoushou omachi kudasai!
example.ja: はい、ただいま伺います。少々お待ちください！
example.english: Yes, I'll be right with you. One moment, please!

notes: Tadaima here means right now, not the I'm-home greeting. Ukagau is the humble verb for come or visit.

src: 保険証をお願いします
ja: 保険証をお願いします
kana: ほけんしょうをおねがいします
use: Clinic or pharmacy reception asks for it when you check in; hand over the card.

example.romaji: hajimete desu ka? hokenshou o onegai shimasu.
example.ja: 初めてですか？保険証をお願いします。
example.english: Is this your first visit? Your insurance card, please.

notes: Many clinics now take the My Number card instead: mainanbaa kaado.

src: お支払いはどうされますか
ja: お支払いはどうされますか
kana: おしはらいはどうされますか
english: how would you like to pay?
use: Asked at the register; answer kaado de, genkin de (cash), or an app name + de.

example.romaji: zenbu de sanzen en desu. oshiharai wa dou saremasu ka?
example.ja: 全部で3000円です。お支払いはどうされますか？
example.english: That's 3,000 yen altogether. How would you like to pay?

notes: Also heard as oshiharai houhou wa? (payment method?).

src: お名前を伺ってもよろしいですか
ja: お名前を伺ってもよろしいですか
kana: おなまえをうかがってもよろしいですか
romaji: onamae o ukagatte mo yoroshii desu ka
use: Reception, phone staff or a booking desk asks it; answer with your family name + desu.

example.romaji: kakunin shimasu node, onamae o ukagatte mo yoroshii desu ka?
example.ja: 確認しますので、お名前を伺ってもよろしいですか？
example.english: May I have your name so I can check?

notes: Ukagau here is the humble verb for ask; a friend would just say namae wa?

english: can I help you?; what do you need?
use: Staff or a receptionist ask it when you walk up, or someone asks it at the door; say what you want.

example.ja: すみません、何かご用ですか？
example.english: Excuse me, can I help you?

notes: Goyou means your business or errand. From a stranger it can sound cool, like what do you want here?

politeJa: 毎度ありがとうございます
english: thanks as always; hi there (shopkeeper's greeting)
use: Shopkeepers say maido arigatou gozaimasu to customers; in Osaka a bare maido! is a friendly hello.

example.romaji: maido! kyou wa nani ni suru?
example.english: Hi there! What'll it be today?

examplePolite.romaji: maido arigatou gozaimasu. mata okoshi kudasai.
examplePolite.ja: 毎度ありがとうございます。またお越しください。
examplePolite.english: Thank you as always. Please come again.

notes: Literally every time. Maido ari is the clipped market-stall version.

src: ご注文は以上でよろしいですか
ja: ご注文は以上でよろしいですか
kana: ごちゅうもんはいじょうでよろしいですか
romaji: gochuumon wa ijou de yoroshii desu ka
english: will that be all?; is that everything?
use: Staff check after you order; answer hai, or add something.

example.romaji: kashikomarimashita. gochuumon wa ijou de yoroshii desu ka?
example.ja: かしこまりました。ご注文は以上でよろしいですか？

notes: Often shortened to ijou de yoroshii desu ka? Ijou means that's all.

use: Convenience-store staff ask about bento and other food; answer onegai shimasu, or daijoubu desu (no thanks).

example.ja: こちらのお弁当、温めますか？
example.english: Shall I heat up this bento?

notes: Also heard as oatatame shimasu ka? Daijoubu desu here means no thanks.

kana: ふくろはおつけしますか
use: Cashiers ask because bags cost a few yen; answer onegai shimasu, or daijoubu desu (no thanks).

example.romaji: fukuro wa otsuke shimasu ka? san en ni narimasu.
example.ja: 袋はお付けしますか？3円になります。
example.english: Do you need a bag? It's 3 yen.

notes: Also heard as fukuro wa goriyou desu ka? or fukuro irimasu ka?

src: お箸はお付けしますか
ja: お箸はお付けしますか
kana: おはしはおつけしますか
use: Asked at convenience stores and takeout counters; answer onegai shimasu, or daijoubu desu (no thanks).

example.romaji: obentou futatsu desu ne. ohashi wa otsuke shimasu ka?
example.ja: お弁当二つですね。お箸はお付けしますか？
example.english: Two bentos, right? Do you need chopsticks?

notes: The same pattern comes for spoons: supuun wa otsuke shimasu ka?

english: is a sticker okay? (instead of a bag)
use: When you buy one small item, the cashier offers to mark it paid with a sticker instead of bagging it; answer hai.

example.romaji: kochira, shiiru de ii desu ka?
example.ja: こちら、シールでいいですか？
example.english: Is a sticker okay for this?

notes: Also heard as teepu de yoroshii desu ka? (tape).

src: ポイントカードはお持ちですか
ja: ポイントカードはお持ちですか
kana: ポイントカードはおもちですか
romaji: pointo kaado wa omochi desu ka
english: do you have a points card?
use: Asked at almost every register; answer nai desu, or hand the card over.

example.romaji: irasshaimase. pointo kaado wa omochi desu ka?
example.ja: いらっしゃいませ。ポイントカードはお持ちですか？
example.english: Hello. Do you have a points card?

notes: Omochi desu ka (do you have?) also comes up for tickets, coupons and receipts.

src: 一括でよろしいですか
ja: 一括でよろしいですか
kana: いっかつでよろしいですか
use: Asked when you pay by credit card, since installments are an option; answer hai.

example.romaji: kaado de desu ne. ikkatsu de yoroshii desu ka?
example.ja: カードでですね。一括でよろしいですか？
example.english: By card, then. In one payment?

notes: Bunkatsu means installments; you almost always want ikkatsu.

src: こちらのレジへどうぞ
ja: こちらのレジへどうぞ
kana: こちらのレジへどうぞ
english: this register, please; I can help you over here
use: A cashier opening another till calls the next customer over; go to that register.

example.romaji: otsugi no okyakusama, kochira no reji e douzo.
example.ja: お次のお客様、こちらのレジへどうぞ。
example.english: Next customer, over at this register, please.

notes: Reji means the cash register or checkout.
